briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Pain, Election Hope: Michigan Operators Eye Relief as National Deals & Psilocybin Momentum Build
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis industry is leaning into the 2026 governor's race and courtroom fights for relief from its 24% wholesale tax, even as Zalympix crowns new statewide champions and distressed farm assets open the door for well-capitalized buyers. Nationally, a DEA rescheduling pause is just a speed bump next to accelerating MSO consolidation and a psilocybin therapy racing toward a 2027 FDA decision.

local.text: Cannabis executives bet on John James for relief
local.text_full: Cannabis executives bet on John James for relief — Michigan's top cannabis executives have endorsed GOP gubernatorial candidate John James over his pledge to cut the state's 24% wholesale weed tax, per state Sen. Jeff Irwin's warning to the industry.
